title: FreqDepthKV: Frequency-Guided Depth Sharing for Robust KV Cache Compression in Long-Context LLM Inference
abstract: Long-context LLM inference is increasingly limited by the memory and bandwidth cost of KV caches, yet aggressive compression can remove the layer-specific evidence needed for retrieval and multi-step reasoning. We introduce FreqDepthKV, an inference-time cache compression method that factorizes adjacent-layer KV states into shared low-frequency depth components and sparse high-frequency residuals. A lightweight online probe assigns attention heads to shared-depth, residual-depth, or exact cache modes according to their contribution to reconstruction-sensitive attention logits, allowing the compression policy to adapt to prompt structure without retraining. Across long-context question answering, needle retrieval, summarization, and code generation benchmarks, FreqDepthKV preserves task accuracy under substantially smaller cache budgets. With a 32k-token prefill window, FreqDepthKV reaches 58.3 Exact Match, 63.0 F1, 32.5 ROUGE-L, and 48.1 pass@1, closely matching full KV while outperforming prior compressed-cache methods. It also improves decoding throughput to 70.4 tokens/s, reduces TTFT to 2.06 seconds, and lowers peak KV memory to 6.2 GB, achieving a 3.9x effective compression ratio.

significance.justification: The paper directly addresses a core bottleneck in long-context LLM inference (KV cache memory/bandwidth) with a method that preserves accuracy while improving throughput and reducing latency, changing architectural decisions for builders deploying such models.

novelty.justification: It introduces a novel frequency-guided depth-sharing factorization for KV caches with an online adaptive probe, a substantial new variation distinct from prior compression techniques like quantization or pruning.

reproducibility.justification: The method is described with algorithmic details (factorization, probe, three cache modes) and evaluated across standard benchmarks, though the paper text does not explicitly state code or artifacts are public.

clarity.justification: The paper is well-written, clearly presenting the problem, method, and comprehensive evaluation across accuracy, speed, and memory metrics with appropriately scoped claims.

topical_fit.justification: The paper is directly in the applied LLM engineering sweet spot, offering a practical inference-time optimization method for builders dealing with long-context LLM deployment challenges.
